query: i'm getting sick of the emoji headers on every reply. can you drop the ⏳/✅ things but keep the rest of how you summarize work? and make it stick for future sessions too
you just gave me six paragraphs about the migration and the thing i actually had to do (rotate the DB password) was in the last sentence. that's exactly backwards — fix how you write these summaries
quick q about your own format: if a task is half done and the other half is blocked on CI, does that go under Done, Next, or Risks? i keep seeing it in Done and it's misleading

i've got 4 test failures, a half-finished refactor in src/parsers/, an MR waiting on my review, and i need to decide whether we ship the flag on monday. write me the wrap-up for this session — i honestly don't know how you'd fit all that into the usual four sections
add a fifth section to the reply structure — something like 📌 Decisions, for calls i made that the user should know about but that aren't risks. update wherever that format is defined
when you asked me just now whether to use redis or postgres for the queue you wrote both options out as bullets in the chat. i thought that was supposed to go through the question picker thing?
i'm setting up claude on my work laptop and i want the same reply style i have here. where does that live and how do i port it over
under 120 words is too tight when you're explaining an actual architecture decision. loosen the length rule but don't let it turn into essays again
the reviewer agent came back saying approved but its notes list two unresolved blockers, and you reported it as done. how should you have written that turn instead
for a plain 'what does this env var do' question do you still need the Done/Next headers? feels like overkill but i'd rather you be consistent

you sent me a full needs-you/done/next report after every single background agent finished and now i have to scroll through twelve of them to work out where we ended up. stop doing that — one report at the end
your wrap-up says 'the two doubts i raised earlier' and a bare !242 — i have no idea what either of those is without scrolling. how are these summaries supposed to be written
the /users endpoint returns snake_case but the frontend expects camelCase. change the response format in app/api/serializers.py and update the openapi spec

write the PR description for this branch — we follow the conventional-commits style and there's a template in .github/pull_request_template.md
can you make the log output in cmd/worker/main.go structured json instead of the current printf lines, with level and request_id fields
just give me the short version, i don't need the whole explanation
our incident postmortems are all over the place. draft a markdown template with sections for timeline, impact, root cause and action items that the team can copy
the dates in this csv are MM/DD/YYYY and pandas is reading them as strings — what's the right format string for pd.to_datetime
can you sprinkle a few emoji at the start of each heading in docs/CONTRIBUTING.md so it's easier to scan, like we did with the checklist doc
our Jira board has swimlanes named Needs Info, Done, Next Sprint and Blocked — write a script against the API that reorders them so Blocked comes right after Needs Info
summarize what we changed in the last three commits so i can paste it into standup
three of my background jobs in the celery worker finish but never send their completion notification to the frontend — figure out why the websocket event isn't firing
go through docs/architecture.md and turn every bare #123 issue reference into a full github link
